records.region: Hudson Bay Lowland, northeastern Manitoba, Canada; coastal drainage east of Hayes River and through the eastern part of Kaskatamagan Sipi Wildlife Management Area.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The complete selected geography is depicted by an independent conservation map, but it does not label this river. Regional Machichi River prose is insufficient to attach that name to this selection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Independent original conservation cartography supports the entire selected river corridor and its Hudson Bay outlet east of Hayes, but does not name the river. Machichi River is only a regional contextual lead. Completed geographic correspondence is therefore held for name scope; accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null, with no automatic or product application.
records.completion_scope: All fourteen selected mainstem parts, the southern opening, intermediate joins, broad lowland passages, and the actual coastal terminal were considered against the independent conservation poster. Ordinary geographic correspondence is complete. The poster has no hydronym on this river, and regional Machichi prose alone does not establish a selected identity. This is a completed name-scope hold, not missing geographic source material.
records.supported_name_scope: No selected-river hydronym established; ordinary selected geography is complete.

scope_limits: Kaskatamagan Sipi is the name of the wildlife management area; the poster does not label this selected river with that name.
Hayes River is a distinct neighbouring labelled river, not the selected course.
Machichi River remains a contextual lead only. Search-discovery labels and incidental excluded naming-service results are not used as substantive evidence.
The absence of a river label on this conservation map does not establish that the river lacks a name.
No exact source point, uniform scalar name, current flow, precise bank or shoreline determination is claimed.

records.region: Texas: West Navidad–Navidad–Lake Texana–Lavaca River corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-river/system identity for the connected selected West Navidad–Navidad–Lake Texana–lower Lavaca route to Lavaca Bay. The Lavaca name is not assigned to every upstream reach or to the reservoir.
records.completion_scope: Four overlapping original maps were visually read across all 33 stored parts of the one selected mainstem, from its chosen headward channel through named confluences, the middle floodplain, reservoir inlet and main body, dam/outlet, lower river and actual coastal endpoint. Two primary agency overview pages support the reservoir and receiving-water relationships. Ordinary connected-corridor correspondence is established. Local bend, dam-position and final mouth-spit shortcuts are explicit generalization limits, not claims of separate channels on each modeled segment.
records.supported_name_scope: West Navidad River above its East Navidad junction; Navidad River downstream through the long inland corridor and reservoir/outlet setting; Lake Texana for the impoundment; Lavaca River for the receiving lower river and estuary. East Navidad River is the joining branch, and Lavaca Bay is the receiver.

records.region: Eastern Victoria Island, Nunavut; Jayko/Jayco lake-and-river drainage to Albert Edward Bay.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the connected selected western feeder, inland lake-and-stream succession, Jayco Lake and its named outlet river to Albert Edward Bay. The lower-river name is not imposed uniformly on the individual inland lakes or every feeder.
records.completion_scope: Bounded ordinary geographic correspondence covers the chosen western opening, all31 selected parts, the intervening lake passages and joins, the continuation beyond the Washburn map edge, Jayco Lake, the outlet river and the actual Albert Edward Bay terminal. The thesis map overlaps the land-resource map and independently continues the eastern corridor; the basin boundary is kept distinct from mapped channels. No material through-link remains unsupported at the requested scale.
records.supported_name_scope: Jayco River is printed in the original field study; the DFO plan pairs Jayko with Jayco River. Jayco Lake and Albert Edward Bay are distinct named waterbodies.

scope_limits: The current formal registry status and legal name boundaries are unverified. DFO’s source-attributed Jayko/Jayco pairing is retained without a gazetteer adjudication.
No separate name is established for the chosen opening or most intermediate lakes and connecting streams; this does not assert that local or official names do not exist.
The western land-resource map and thesis are historical, generalized sources. Exact banks, lake entry/exit vertices, confluence vertices and present shoreline positions are outside the result.
The field study depicts a historical fishing weir near the outlet. Its present existence or operation is not asserted, and it is not treated as a reservoir or a distinct managed through-connection.
No current discharge, seasonal passability, perennial-flow condition or operational hydraulic connection is established.

records.region: Northern Baja California and the Tijuana border drainage
records.material_pending_reason: The acquired maps do not establish the continuous reservoir-to-border urban passage or the selected westward terminal fragment. The directly mapped Tijuana River estuary and Pacific mouth follow a different corridor north of the border.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Tijuana River is directly labelled on the mapped United States receiving reach and estuary. It is not established as a representative identity for the entire selected system because the selected lower connections remain unsupported. The other names are bounded upstream reach candidates.
records.completion_scope: Both selected fragments and all stored parts were considered. The chosen opening, upper named reaches, joins and reservoir passage have ordinary-scale correspondence. The urban lower connection and selected coastal continuation remain genuine source-material gaps; map coverage alone is not treated as established hydrological correspondence.
records.supported_name_scope: Tijuana River is directly labelled on the mapped United States receiving reach and estuary. It is not established as a representative identity for the entire selected system because the selected lower connections remain unsupported. The other names are bounded upstream reach candidates.

scope_limits: The unlabelled chosen opening is not assigned the nearby Arroyo San Pedro name.
Distinct named reaches are retained without exact name-transition boundaries.
The unsupported terminal continuation is a material correspondence gap rather than a completed naming-scope hold. No claim is made about why the selected model follows that route.
Historical map symbols do not establish current discharge, permanent flow, reservoir levels, water quality, operations, exact banks or an official surveyed source or mouth.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
